answer: An inaudible chirp sent between two nearby devices can bound their distance, because the arrival delay proves the phones are within a couple of metres of each other. The verifier issues a random chirp, the second device records it, and the measured delay is checked against the speed of sound, so a remote farm cannot pretend to be beside anyone. A canyon of fake locations collapses when every pair must be physically close, no software can forge a shorter flight time, and the pearl of a true measurement is that physics, not a claim, sets the limit.
